**Verdict**
Modi in 2024 shows real institution-building in service delivery, digital public infrastructure, grievance redress, and some rights-targeted schemes. The weakness is durability and insulation: most of the positive evidence is official self-reporting, while independent reporting shows persistent politicization of information space, patronage-shaped spending, and failure to protect equal standing in several crises. Overall: mixed, leaning positive on administrative capacity, but not enough to say the institutions were clearly protected from personal-rule dynamics.

**Accepted Claims**
- **AI-assisted CPGRAMS and last-mile grievance redress** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions | Date: 18 Jan 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1997326&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: The government funded AI-assisted grievance redress, process re-engineering, and “last mile” service delivery. This is strong evidence of a reusable administrative platform rather than one-off patronage, and it is the clearest positive sign for durable state capacity. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **ABDM / ABHA digital health infrastructure** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare | Date: 28 Sep 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=153215&lang=1&reg=3 | Summary: The government highlighted expanded Ayushman Bharat coverage, U-WIN, new medical seats, and digital health registries. If these systems endure, they are the kind of standardized health institutions that can survive beyond a single leader’s personal network. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **ABDM scale-up and linked health records** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare | Date: 17 Dec 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2085201&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: The government said ABDM had built large-scale digital health infrastructure, including ABHA accounts and linked records. This points to institutionalized service delivery and data continuity, not just discretionary benefits. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **Digital Agriculture Mission and farmer registries** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare | Date: 2 Sep 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2050966&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: The mission used digital public infrastructure, crop estimation, and data-driven support for farmers. This is evidence of an institutionalized delivery stack for a major welfare sector, though the evidence is official self-reporting. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **Women-centered rural institutions and differentiated housing support** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Rural Development; PTI via ThePrint | Date: 30 Jul 2024; 9 Aug 2024; 31 Dec 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2039162&lang=2&reg=48 ; https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2043919&lang=2&reg=48 ; https://theprint.in/india/women-empowerment-remained-in-focus-for-rural-development-ministry-in-2024/2425889/ | Summary: DAY-NRLM mobilized more than 10 crore rural women into self-help groups, and PMAY-G was extended with region-sensitive assistance and women’s ownership emphasis. These are durable-looking social institutions because they are programmatic, large-scale, and not obviously tied to personal favoritism. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **Minority empowerment and anti-atrocity administration** | Publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs; Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Minority Affairs | Date: 2 Jul 2024; 7 Aug 2024; 11 Dec 2024 | URL: https://www.mha.gov.in/en/commoncontent/advisories-0 ; https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2042759&lang=1&reg=3 ; https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2083334&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: The Home Ministry issued 2024 advisories on anti-atrocity implementation for SC/ST protections, while minority-affairs releases described scholarships and PM VIKAS/Nai Roshni training for minority women. This is positive evidence for equal-access institutions, though mostly from official releases and not outcome audits. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8
- **New criminal-law rollout and digital case tools** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Home Affairs | Date: 30 Dec 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2088945&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: The government described the new criminal laws as victim-centric and highlighted e-Sakshya, Nyaya Setu, Nyaya Shruti, and e-Summon. This suggests an attempt to build more durable justice institutions, but the evidence is official self-description rather than independent proof of durable depoliticization. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8
- **Coalition-targeted post-election budget spending** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 23 Jul 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-spends-billions-on-jobs-key-allies-in-first-budget-after-election/2187546/ | Summary: Reuters reported that the first post-election budget aimed to win back voters and retain coalition support, with more than $5 billion directed to coalition-led states. This weakens the durability claim because public money was visibly being used for political management, not just neutral institution-building. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **Coalition bargaining over funds and cabinet positions** | Publisher: Reuters via Investing.com | Date: 6 Jun 2024 | URL: https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/modis-appeal-clouded-in-india-election-by-prices-jobs-graft-survey-says-3472931 | Summary: Regional allies demanded more funds and cabinet jobs as coalition talks began. That is evidence of patronage-style bargaining at the center of government formation, which cuts against a clean institutionalization story. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7
- **Opaque electoral finance and BJP advantage** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 16 Feb 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/explainer-what-were-indias-electoral-bonds-and-how-did-they-power-modis-party/1969006/ | Summary: Reuters described the electoral-bonds system as allowing unlimited anonymous donations, with the BJP the largest beneficiary. That is counterevidence because opaque money pipelines make durable, impartial institutions less likely. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **Fact-check unit, WhatsApp outreach, and regulatory pressure on information space** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint; Election Commission of India via Hindustan Times; Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | Date: 21 Mar 2024; 21 Mar 2024; 17 Jun 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-puts-on-hold-unit-for-fact-checking-online-content-about-govt/2009612/ ; https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/election-commission-to-it-ministry-stop-sending-viksit-bharat-messages-on-whatsapp-101711006490551.html ; https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/india | Summary: The government created a fact-checking unit to police online content about government business, the Election Commission had to stop government-branded WhatsApp outreach, and Reuters Institute noted broad new laws and regulatory powers that critics saw as threatening press freedom. This is negative evidence for durable institutions because it shows centralizing and politicizing state communication rather than insulating it. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8
- **Communal rhetoric and failure to protect vulnerable communities** | Publisher: Human Rights Watch; Amnesty International; Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 11 Jan 2024; 14 Aug 2024; 16 Jul 2024; 10 Sep 2024 | URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/india-increased-abuses-against-minorities-critics ; https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/14/india-hate-speech-fueled-modis-election-campaign ; https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/india-authorities-missing-in-action-amid-ongoing-violence-and-impunity-in-manipur-state-new-testimonies/ ; https://theprint.in/india/internet-suspended-in-parts-of-indias-manipur-as-students-clash-with-police/2261451/ | Summary: HRW and Amnesty reported minority stigmatization, hate speech, the Manipur crisis, and coercive responses such as shutdowns and curfews. This is counterevidence because durable social institutions should protect equal standing and basic security across groups, and the 2024 record does not show that reliably. | Question IDs: 6B.9, 6B.8, 3B.1

**Search Gap**
- The strongest positive evidence is mostly official self-reporting from ministries, not independent implementation audits.
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence that these institutions were formally insulated from Modi’s personal discretion, budget control, or coalition bargaining.
- I also did not find a clean, independent before/after assessment showing that these systems would clearly survive a leadership change without political weakening.
